messages:
mike: FYI — seeing a cluster of customer tickets about 5xx on the hosted API starting ~2026-02-28 11:42 UTC. Most are 502/504 gateway errors. Customers report failures against /v1/generate and some session auth failures. Sample error payload:

customer snippet: "error: upstream returned 502 (control-plane)"

mike: I pulled a few request IDs from logs: x-request-id=rp_00a1f3c, rp_00a1f45, rp_00a1f4b — all are returning 502 with message: "control-plane: routing-policy timeout"

mike: Repro (customer cURL):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' 
  -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"hello"}' 
```
response: 502, body: "service error; upstream=control-plane; code=E_ROUTE_TIMEOUT"

aisha: thanks, digging in. Can you paste a full raw response/headers for one rp id? I want the trace id for our trace sampling. Also which region? (us-west-2?)

mike: region is us-west-2 for these three. full headers for rp_00a1f45:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:44:01 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: rp_00a1f45
X-Trace-ID: trace-9b2f
Server: redwood-gateway/1.3.4

{"error":"control-plane: routing-policy timeout", "code":"E_ROUTE_TIMEOUT"}
```

opsbot: Incident metrics alert: control_plane.routing_policy.error_rate > 5% for 3m in us-west-2 (fired at 2026-02-28T11:43:30Z)

tom: I'm looking at prometheus — confirmed spike in 11:40-11:46 UTC for control-plane services. Two hotspots: session-service (auth/session) errors and routing-policy-service timeouts. Query I ran: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=control-plane,code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (service)` — routing-policy and sessions are highest.

tom: Also seeing increased p95 latency to config-db (our config-store) from routing-policy pod logs: slow queries ~600-900ms and occasional connection pool exhaustion.

leo: I'm on the DB side — Aurora replicas in us-west-2 show elevated replica lag and CPU spike correlating with the window. There were a burst of schema-read-heavy requests (policy resolution) from routing-policy around the same time. Some queries weren't using the policy cache due to TTL expiry together.

aisha: hypothesis: config DB slow/conn issues -> routing-policy falls back to sync lookups -> timeouts -> gateway surfaces 502/504 to clients. Also session-service hitting DB for user sessions and returning 5xx auth errors.

aisha: mitigation options: 1) enable routing-policy local cache fallback (force cache use for 10m), 2) increase DB connection pool size temporarily, 3) route traffic to other regions for affected customers, 4) return 429/503 with Retry-After instead of 502 to make client retries cleaner. Prefer a1 + 2 short-term.

leo: I can bump the config-store max connections by +40 and increase timeout to 5s for next 15 minutes. Will monitor. Command I used: `rctl config-store set --region us-west-2 --max-conns 360 --query-timeout 5000`

aisha: I'm going to flip the routing-policy fallback flag in the control-plane so gateways will use cached routing policies when DB lookups fail. Patch command (console):
```bash
redwoodctl patch controlplane --component routing-policy --set feature.cache_fallback=true --region us-west-2 --reason "hotfix: configdb timeouts"
```

deploy-bot: Started rollout: controlplane/routing-policy v2.14.6 -> canary (us-west-2) by aisha at 11:48 UTC

mike: after the rollback/fallback flip we started seeing errors drop — support tickets stopped escalating. Affected customers confirmed degraded but working (some increased latency, fewer hard 502s).

tom: I've opened an alert for connection pool exhaustion and added an automatic fallback path to serve default routing when DB is unreachable. We'll follow up with a postmortem. Owner: tom, aisha, leo.

aisha: immediate follow-ups:
- add exponential backoff and Retry-After handling in gateway for control-plane 5xx
- add per-service SLIs that trigger earlier scaling of config-store replicas
- run a query audit: find heavy policy-resolution queries and add caching or indexes

mike: billing note — short investigation: request logs for rp_* show these failed requests were not charged (status != 200); billing team will confirm final decision. tagging @billing for confirmation.

leo: DB-side logs I pulled (filtered):
```sql
-- slow query sample
SELECT policy_blob FROM routing_policies WHERE tenant_id = 't_12345' AND revision <= 100 ORDER BY revision DESC LIMIT 1; -- 842ms
```

aisha: thanks everyone. Creating follow-up in #incidents with timeline + action items. I'll add a canary-test to ensure cache_fallback won't drift traffic silently.

mike: closing loop with support: sent update to affected customers and set auto-retry guidance. Will add a short KB entry: "5xx caused by control-plane config DB timeouts -> what to check". React with :white_check_mark: when you have ownership of your action items.
